correctness.rationale: A valid height word of length n uses precisely {0,...,h}; each such word becomes a distinguished edge in the (n-1)-overlap digraph. Complete vertices are all W_{n-1}; incomplete vertices have indegree and outdegree one, and forced paths end at complete vertices in at most n rotations. Contracting forced corridors preserves cyclic edge-distinguished Euler tours. The reduced core has |W_{n-1}| vertices; directed matrix-tree/BEST give U_n=det(L_root) product_v(d_v-1)!, where the factorial product is the stated Stirling-number expression. Independently implemented height-word enumeration, full overlap digraph, forced contraction, exact SymPy integer cofactor and factorial product for n=2,3,4,5. Reproduced U=(1,8,113192681472,6214252301172599252248681937277855126085721393995382376959963220030028306692926790213752299261892430397440); at n=5, 541 original word-edges contract to 308 distinguished arcs on 75 core vertices, tau=27571102170646823740986252600397906575360 and the exact degree histogram {2:1,3:14,4:36,5:24}. Full finite census established with exact determinant, no extrapolation to n>=6.

originality.rationale: Best of knowledge: Horan–Hurlbert 2012/2013 prove existence of weak-order universal cycles via the same height-word overlap graph; Sawada–Wong and Sawada–Gabrić develop successor rules, random uniform sampling, and general arborescence methods. Primary text does not supply these evaluated exact U_4/U_5 multiplicities or the concrete 75-vertex core certificate. Standard BEST/matrix-tree derivation is prior mathematics; novel surviving finite invariant is the fully evaluated enumeration and forced-corridor graph reduction at order five. A previously unindexed Euler-tour or integer table remains a real priority risk.
residual_risks: An earlier not-indexed exact weak-order universal-cycle table or enumeration in supplementary combinatorial software could cover U4/U5.
This census stops at n=5 and does not count cycles modulo alphabet relabeling or reversal; the general contraction does not evaluate arbitrary-n cofactor.
